answer: A reputation ledger tied to staked work makes sybil attacks expensive: each agent identity must post a bond before joining the market, and the bond is slashed when peers flag fraud. New identities start on a knoll of low trust, limited to small jobs, and must climb a trellis of verified, attested tasks to earn higher-value work. The thread connecting an agent's past jobs, payments and attestations is public, so spinning up fresh identities means starting over with zero reputation and fresh stake, while an established identity has real value to lose.
